sources.citation: Nourzaei, Maryam. 2024. Kholosi. In Haig et al. (eds.), Post-predicate elements in the Western Asian Transition Zone, 175-195. Berlin: Language Science Press. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.14266341
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Jadgali stress; Jadgali is mentioned only as the other Indo-Aryan outlier in Iran (location, no contact with Kholosi, retains split ergativity). Describes Kholosi (khol1240), not Jadgali.

sources.citation: ELAR deposit: Nourzaei, Maryam. 2023. Documentation of the Jadgali language. Endangered Languages Archive, hdl:2196/m90p1784-6090-2r4m-861n-e5o46432717n
sources.note: Deposit page lists 13 audio recordings (narratives, elicited wordlists) and 1 photo; no grammar sketch or phonology notes deposited.

sources.citation: Al Jahdhami, Said. 2015. Minority Languages in Oman. Anglisticum Journal 4(10): 105-112.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3.10 'Zadjali' (the Omani Jadgali community) is one sociolinguistic paragraph; it states that resources on the language 'are indeed impossible to find'.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. 1919. Linguistic Survey of India VIII.1 (Sindhi and Lahnda) [local djvu text ]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only an identity remark: in Baluchistan Lahnda and Sindhi are called 'Jatki' or, by the Baloch, 'Jadgali'/'Jagdali'; no description of the Makran Jadgali variety and nothing on its stress.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Jadgali language' and Wikipedia (fa) 'زبان جدگالی' (wikitext downloaded)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. fa.wikipedia names two Iranian studies without authors: 'بررسی اشتراکات و اختلافات آوایی و دستوری زبان اردو و گویش جدگالی' and 'توصیف جامع زبان جدگالی' (unverifiable from here).

sources.citation: Nourzaei, Maryam. (in preparation / ELDP-ELAR project 0732) Grammar sketch or first description of Jadgali based on the ELAR corpus 'Documentation of the Jadgali language' (Uppsala/CNRS).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Nourzaei is the only linguist currently documenting Jadgali (ELAR deposit 2023; ORCID lists no Jadgali publication yet); any forthcoming sketch would be the first modern primary description and would supersede everything above.

sources.citation: Al Jahdhami, Said. 2017. Zadjali: The dying language. International Journal of Language and Linguistics 4(3): 49-54.

sources.note: Glottolog-typed comparative/wordlist paper on the Omani Jadgali (Zadjali) variety; may include brief phonological notes. Formerly open at ijllnet.com/journals/Vol_4_No_3_September_2017/ (domain now parked); retrievable via the Internet Archive when archive.org is reachable.

sources.citation: Bashir, Elena. 2016. Contact and convergence: Baluchistan. In H. H. Hock & E. Bashir (eds.), The Languages and Linguistics of South Asia: A comprehensive guide, 271-284. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.

sources.note: Areal overview that treats Jadgali among Balochistan languages; low chance of a stress remark but the only handbook coverage.

sources.citation: Delforooz, Behrooz Barjasteh. 2008. A sociolinguistic survey among the Jadgal in Iranian Balochistan. In C. Jahani, A. Korn & P. Titus (eds.), The Baloch and Others: Linguistic, historical and socio-political perspectives on pluralism in Balochistan, 23-43. Wiesbaden: Reichert.

sources.note: The one scholarly publication devoted to Jadgali (Glottolog's only ref); may contain a short structural overview with transcription conventions that mark stress.

sources.citation: 'توصیف جامع زبان جدگالی' [A comprehensive description of the Jadgali language] -- Iranian MA/PhD thesis named (without author) on fa.wikipedia; presumably University of Sistan and Baluchestan or similar, in Persian
